top_choice_rationale: P001 (B001, Helpman and Melitz) rests on a single, identifiable mechanism: selection of heterogeneous firms into exporting and foreign investment, with reallocation across firms as a channel for the gains from trade. Melitz (2003) and Helpman, Melitz and Yeaple (2004) produced testable implications, including exports-versus-FDI sorting, and firm-level data from many countries have tested them for more than twenty years. Where the baseline model failed in detail, the literature extended it and kept the selection logic. That is the maturity I weigh most: a clear mechanism, falsifiable predictions and accumulated evidence. The main risk is attribution. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, and Redding's quantitative work, are not credited on this entry, and whether a two-name award is too narrow depends on how the discovery is defined. I judge that the citation can be confined to selection and reallocation, with the empirical precursors acknowledged in the scientific background. It should not claim settled welfare magnitudes or the whole firm-level trade literature. The convergence of the round-2 files is not evidence of merit, and I did not rely on it. The slate offers only this award or no award. The achievement is mature and clearly attributable, and I judge the attribution risk manageable, so I rank it above P000.
recusal_note: None apparent from profile for Helpman or Melitz. My co-authors and ties (Uppsala, IFAU, Stockholm University) are in labour and education economics, and none is credited on B001. I overlapped institutionally, not as a co-author, with the IIES macro group (Hassler, Krusell) at Stockholm University. My field is adjacent to the empirical, credibility-oriented use of firm-level data, which may incline me toward B001. Disclosed and not adjudicated.
